newsitem.title: Australia: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: DOWNER WELCOMES CHEMICAL WEAPONS CONVENTION

Foreign Minister, Alexander Downer, says it's important that Russia and the United States, as declared holders of chemical weapons, move quickly to ratify the Chemical Weapons Convention. The convention, for a total ban on chemical weapons, has reached its trigger point, having been ratified by 65 countries, including Australia.
This means it will come into force next April.
Mr Downer says the convention is a central pillar of global and regional disarmament, and is the first treaty to outlaw an entire class of weapons of mass destruction.
PM SUPPORTS SMALL BUSINESS GUIDELINES
The Prime Minister says the report of the Small Business Deregulation Task Force, released today, goes a long way to fulfilling his promise to cut red tape for small business.
The report calls for a simplification of the tax system, and a streamlining of government regulations.
John Howard says the report's recommendation to simplify fringe benefits tax is one he's particularly welcomed, and says he wishes he could abolish the tax once and for all.
The report's also been backed by key industry groups who see it as taking a common sense approach to stimulating small business.
KENNETT WANTS TO ARRANGE MEETING WITH HANSON
Victorian Premier, Jeff Kennett, says he's hopeful he can arrange a private meeting with Independent Federal M-P, Pauline Hanson.
Mr Kennett says he and Ms Hanson probably have a lot in common, both being outspoken, and says he hopes any talks the pair arrange will be positive.
Mr Kennett says Ms Hanson's comments on Asian immigration and Aboriginal people could damage Australia.
REPORT FORECASTS SLIGHT RISE IN TOURISM
A major report on the tourism industry is forecasting a two percent increase in domestic tourism in Australia during the next decade.
The Tourism Forecasting Council has released the report at a National Tourism Conference in Perth.
It estimates the number of nights spent by tourists in Australia will grow by nearly one hundred and 38 million .
The report also indicates the number of Australians travelling for business will increase.
Council chairman, Sir Frank Moore says the forecast signalled an end to a downturn in domestic tourism experienced in the early 1990s.
